# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)

-- A sheet's pools: a trimmed name, at most once per sheet. A pool's members are people on the sheet,
-- each at most once per pool, with a share percent (two decimals, more than 0.00, at most 100.00).
-- A person can be in several pools.
CREATE TABLE pool (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet(id),
    name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (sheet_id, name)
);
CREATE TABLE pool_member (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    pool_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES pool(id),
    person_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES person(id),
    share DECIMAL(5, 2) NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (pool_id, person_id)
);
-- A sheet's pot, with two decimals, not dated: shared out as cuts among a balanced pool's members. Null: none.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN pot DECIMAL(19, 2);
-- A pool member may be another pool on the sheet instead of a person: exactly one of person_id and
-- member_pool_id is set. A pool is a member of at most one pool.
ALTER TABLE pool_member ALTER COLUMN person_id SET NULL;
ALTER TABLE pool_member ADD COLUMN member_pool_id BIGINT REFERENCES pool(id);
ALTER TABLE pool_member ADD CONSTRAINT pool_member_pool_once UNIQUE (member_pool_id);
-- A pool membership may carry a from-date and a to-date (both optional, the to-date not before the
-- from-date). A member whose dates do not include the sheet's today is left out of the pool's total
-- share, its balance and its cuts.
ALTER TABLE pool_member ADD COLUMN from_date DATE;
ALTER TABLE pool_member ADD COLUMN to_date DATE;
-- The sheet's today when a pool, and when a pool member, was added (null: from the beginning of
-- time), so the pools can be read as of a date.
ALTER TABLE pool ADD COLUMN added_on DATE;
ALTER TABLE pool_member ADD COLUMN added_on DATE;

-- Every pot set is recorded in the settings history (key pot, no from-date, '' for none).
INSERT INTO setting_history (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value, set_on)
    SELECT id, 'pot', NULL, CAST(pot AS VARCHAR), DATE '0001-01-01' FROM sheet WHERE pot IS NOT NULL;
-- A sheet's dated settings: each value a figure setting takes from a date. The value in force on a
-- date is the one with the latest from-date on or before it; before every from-date the setting has
-- its starting value (floor 1.00, late percent 0.00, terms 14; none for the others). Keys:
-- clerk-limit, floor, terms, late-pct, terms-A, terms-B, terms-C, cap. A blank value is "none"
-- (no clerk limit, no cap, a grade on the sheet's terms).
CREATE TABLE setting_value (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet(id),
    setting_key VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE NOT NULL,
    setting_value VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date)
);
-- The values already set carry over from the sheet's today.
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)
    SELECT id, 'floor', today, CAST(due_floor AS VARCHAR) FROM sheet WHERE due_floor <> 1.00;
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)
    SELECT id, 'terms', today, CAST(terms AS VARCHAR) FROM sheet WHERE terms <> 14;
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)
    SELECT id, 'late-pct', today, CAST(late_pct AS VARCHAR) FROM sheet WHERE late_pct <> 0.00;
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)
    SELECT id, 'clerk-limit', today, CAST(clerk_limit AS VARCHAR) FROM sheet WHERE clerk_limit IS NOT NULL;
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)

I added the per-period cut history to the pools, and `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 tests.

Each pool member's line now shows one extra cut for every period whose to-date is on or before the sheet's today. Each one is labelled `pool-cut-<period>` and they're ordered by from-date. The value is the member's cut as it stood at the end of that period: the pools, members, pot and holds as they were then, with that day as the sheet's today. It's empty when there was no cut. Crew pools get this too. No database change was needed, because the store already keeps the dated history the "as of" read uses.

- **Server:** I moved the existing pool-and-cut calculation in `pool/RespondWithPools.java` into a `read(...)` method that takes a "today" and an as-of date. The endpoint runs it once for now and once for each ended period, using that period's to-date. Each member in the response now carries a `periodCuts` list of period name and cut (new `PeriodCut.java`, plus a new field on `PoolMemberResponse`). It's a list rather than a map so the order holds even if a period name looks like a number.
- **Front end:** `features/pools/pools.ts` has the new field, and `features/pools/pools.slot.tsx` shows the extra cuts after the member's current cut.

Some behaviour the request didn't spell out:
- A period whose to-date is still after today gets no element at all, rather than an empty one.
- A member who joined after a period ended shows an empty cut for that period.
- A member who has since left a pool isn't listed, so their old cuts aren't shown.

The pools endpoint now repeats the full pool calculation once per ended period, so a sheet with many periods will load its pools more slowly.
